covers: The 16 register offsets of the Motorola MC68681 DUART, a read and a write meaning apiece

entries.name: MR1A/MR2A read
entries.description: Reads mode register 1 or 2 of channel A, whichever the mode pointer selects.
entries.behaviour: With the pointer at MR1 the read returns MR1A and moves the pointer to MR2; every later read returns MR2A and leaves it there. Reads and writes share the one pointer. The reset-pointer command (CRA command 1) sends it back to MR1, and reset leaves it at MR1.

entries.name: MR1A/MR2A write
entries.description: Mode registers of channel A: MR1 sets data bits, parity, block-error mode and the receive interrupt source; MR2 sets stop bits and the loopback mode.
entries.behaviour: Pointer at MR1: stores MR1, then moves to MR2. MR1: bits 0-1 data bits less 5, 3-4 parity (0 on, 1 forced, 2 none), 2 odd or mark, 5 block errors, 6 FIFO-full interrupt. MR2: bits 2-3 stop (2 one and a half, 3 two), 6-7 mode: 1 echo, 3 remote (THR writes drop), 2 local loop.

entries.name: SRA
entries.description: Status register of channel A: receiver, transmitter and error flags.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 received break (MAME sets it only in loopback), 6 framing, 5 parity, 4 overrun, 3 transmitter empty, 2 transmitter ready, 1 FIFO full (three), 0 receiver ready. Bits 5 to 7 belong to the FIFO head and clear on its read unless MR1 bit 5 is set. A fifth unread character sets overrun until a reset command.

entries.name: CSRA
entries.description: Clock select of channel A: low nibble for the transmitter, high nibble for the receiver, mapped to a baud rate by a table that ACR bit 7 picks.
entries.behaviour: Codes 0 to 12 pick a rate, ACR bit 7 clear: 50 110 134 200 300 600 1200 1050 2400 4800 7200 9600 38400, set: 75 110 134 150 300 600 1200 2000 2400 4800 1800 9600 19200. 13 follows the counter. 14 and 15: IP3 clock over 16 and direct if ACR bit 7 is clear, else no rate.

entries.name: BRG test
entries.description: Not a readable register: this offset is the command register A, and a read here is the baud rate generator test.
entries.behaviour: MAME returns 0xFF and changes nothing, since no case handles it; the source's header comment says the command register offsets should never be read. The xr68c681 instead returns ISR ANDed with IMR here (MISR).

entries.name: CRA
entries.description: Command register of channel A: enables and disables its receiver and transmitter and runs one command.
entries.behaviour: Bit 0 enables the receiver, bit 1 disables it, bit 2 enables the transmitter, bit 3 disables it, bits 4 to 6 are the command and bit 7 is ignored. The fields combine in one byte; see the commands dictionary. The byte is kept so that bit 2 only enables on a rising edge from the previous write.

entries.name: RHRA
entries.description: Receive holding register of channel A: pops the oldest received character.
entries.behaviour: Returns the head of the FIFO, which holds four characters though the full flag rises at three; an empty FIFO returns 0. A fifth character sets overrun and overwrites the tail. The next character's errors load into SR, bits 5 to 7 clearing first unless MR1 bit 5 is set, and receiver ready clears when the FIFO empties.

entries.name: THRA
entries.description: Transmit holding register of channel A: the next byte to send.
entries.behaviour: The byte is discarded unless transmitter ready (SR bit 2) is set, which needs CR to enable the transmitter. Otherwise ready and empty clear and the byte starts at once or waits in the holding register. Ready returns after the start bit or when the held byte moves on; local loopback feeds the receiver, not TxD.

entries.name: IPCR
entries.description: Input port change register: which of IP0 to IP3 changed and their levels.
entries.behaviour: Bits 7 to 4 are the change flags of IP3 to IP0, bits 3 to 0 the levels of IP3 to IP0 as of the last change on any of them. The read clears bits 7 to 4 and ISR bit 7. IP4 to IP6 never reach this register.

entries.name: ACR
entries.description: Auxiliary control register: baud table, counter/timer mode and clock, and the IP0 to IP3 change interrupt enables.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 picks the baud table, bits 3-0 enable change interrupts of IP3-IP0, bit 6 selects timer (1) or counter mode; changing it starts or stops the timer. Bits 5-4: counter 1 TxCA, 2 TxCB, 3 clock/16; timer 3 clock/16; else the device clock. Re-reads both CSRs; sets ISR bit 7 if a pending IPCR flag is enabled.

entries.name: ISR
entries.description: Interrupt status register: what is asking for an interrupt.
entries.behaviour: Bits 7 to 0: input change, delta break B, receive B, transmit ready B, counter ready, delta break A, receive A, transmit ready A; receive is receiver ready or FIFO full per MR1 bit 6. Bit 7 clears on an IPCR read, bit 3 on a stop-counter read, bits 2 and 6 by reset-break-change. Delta break sets only in loopback.

entries.name: IMR
entries.description: Interrupt mask register: which ISR bits drive the interrupt output.
entries.behaviour: Bits match ISR bits. The interrupt line is active while ISR ANDed with IMR is nonzero, and the write re-evaluates it at once. Reset clears the mask.

entries.name: CTU
entries.description: High byte of the counter/timer's remaining count.
entries.behaviour: Returns bits 8 to 15 of the ticks left, counted at the clock ACR selects. There is no latch, so reading CTU and CTL separately can give a torn value.

entries.name: CTUR
entries.description: High byte of the counter/timer preset.
entries.behaviour: Stored as bits 8 to 15 of the preset. It takes effect at the next start-counter read or timer reload, not on a running count.

entries.name: CTL
entries.description: Low byte of the counter/timer's remaining count.
entries.behaviour: Returns bits 0 to 7 of the ticks left, counted at the clock ACR selects. There is no latch, so reading CTU and CTL separately can give a torn value.

entries.name: CTLR
entries.description: Low byte of the counter/timer preset.
entries.behaviour: Stored as bits 0 to 7 of the preset. A preset of 0 counts as 1 when the counter or timer starts. It takes effect at the next start-counter read or timer reload.

entries.name: MR1B/MR2B read
entries.description: Reads mode register 1 or 2 of channel B, whichever the mode pointer selects.
entries.behaviour: With the pointer at MR1 the read returns MR1B and moves the pointer to MR2; every later read returns MR2B and leaves it there. Reads and writes share the one pointer. The reset-pointer command (CRB command 1) sends it back to MR1, and reset leaves it at MR1.

entries.name: MR1B/MR2B write
entries.description: Mode registers of channel B: MR1 sets data bits, parity, block-error mode and the receive interrupt source; MR2 sets stop bits and the loopback mode.
entries.behaviour: Pointer at MR1: stores MR1, then moves to MR2. MR1: bits 0-1 data bits less 5, 3-4 parity (0 on, 1 forced, 2 none), 2 odd or mark, 5 block errors, 6 FIFO-full interrupt. MR2: bits 2-3 stop (2 one and a half, 3 two), 6-7 mode: 1 echo, 3 remote (THR writes drop), 2 local loop.

entries.name: SRB
entries.description: Status register of channel B: receiver, transmitter and error flags.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 received break (MAME sets it only in loopback), 6 framing, 5 parity, 4 overrun, 3 transmitter empty, 2 transmitter ready, 1 FIFO full (three), 0 receiver ready. Bits 5 to 7 belong to the FIFO head and clear on its read unless MR1 bit 5 is set. A fifth unread character sets overrun until a reset command.

entries.name: CSRB
entries.description: Clock select of channel B: low nibble for the transmitter, high nibble for the receiver, mapped to a baud rate by a table that ACR bit 7 picks.
entries.behaviour: Codes 0 to 12 pick a rate, ACR bit 7 clear: 50 110 134 200 300 600 1200 1050 2400 4800 7200 9600 38400, set: 75 110 134 150 300 600 1200 2000 2400 4800 1800 9600 19200. 13 follows the counter. 14 and 15: IP5 clock over 16 and direct if ACR bit 7 is clear, else no rate.

entries.name: 1X/16X test
entries.description: Test register offset, read as a fixed value.
entries.behaviour: Returns 0x61 with no side effect; the source notes the old 68681 gave that value and an Apollo machine relies on it.

entries.name: CRB
entries.description: Command register of channel B: enables and disables its receiver and transmitter and runs one command.
entries.behaviour: Bit 0 enables the receiver, bit 1 disables it, bit 2 enables the transmitter, bit 3 disables it, bits 4 to 6 are the command and bit 7 is ignored. The fields combine in one byte; see the commands dictionary. The byte is kept so that bit 2 only enables on a rising edge from the previous write.

entries.name: RHRB
entries.description: Receive holding register of channel B: pops the oldest received character.
entries.behaviour: Returns the head of the FIFO, which holds four characters though the full flag rises at three; an empty FIFO returns 0. A fifth character sets overrun and overwrites the tail. The next character's errors load into SR, bits 5 to 7 clearing first unless MR1 bit 5 is set, and receiver ready clears when the FIFO empties.

entries.name: THRB
entries.description: Transmit holding register of channel B: the next byte to send.
entries.behaviour: The byte is discarded unless transmitter ready (SR bit 2) is set, which needs CR to enable the transmitter. Otherwise ready and empty clear and the byte starts at once or waits in the holding register. Ready returns after the start bit or when the held byte moves on; local loopback feeds the receiver, not TxD.

entries.name: IVR read
entries.description: Interrupt vector register: the vector handed out at interrupt acknowledge.
entries.behaviour: Returns IVR, which resets to 0x0F, and a bus read does not count as an acknowledge. On the scn2681 this offset reads 0xFF.

entries.name: IVR write
entries.description: Sets the interrupt vector register.
entries.behaviour: Stores the byte, taken from the mc68681 and xr68c681 only; the scn2681 ignores a write here. The vector is returned by a read of this offset and by the driver's interrupt acknowledge call.

entries.name: IP
entries.description: Input port: the levels of IP0 to IP6, with bit 7 always set.
entries.behaviour: Bits 0 to 6 come from the bound input callback, else from the levels pushed to the ipN_w handlers. Bit 7 always reads 1. On the mc68681 bit 6 is /IACK: 0 after an interrupt acknowledge while an interrupt is pending, else 1; the scn2681 returns IP6 there.

entries.name: OPCR
entries.description: Output port configuration: what drives OP3 and OP4 to OP7.
entries.behaviour: Bits 3-2 equal 01 make OP3 the counter/timer output: counter ready sets it, stop clears it, timer mode toggles it per expiry. Bits 4 to 7 make OP4 to OP7 follow ISR bits 1, 5, 0 and 4. Bits 0-1 and other values of bits 2-3 are unused.

entries.name: start counter
entries.description: Starting the counter/timer: a read of this offset does it.
entries.behaviour: Counter mode loads the preset (0 counts as 1), counts down, sets ISR bit 3 at zero and goes on from 0xFFFF. Timer mode also clears the square-wave phase, then ISR bit 3 sets every second expiry, so a full period is twice the preset. The read returns 0xFF.

entries.name: set output bits
entries.description: Sets output port bits: each 1 in the byte sets that OPR bit.
entries.behaviour: OPR is ORed with the byte and the output callback receives OPR inverted, so a set bit means a low pin. A 0 in the byte changes nothing.

entries.name: stop counter
entries.description: Stopping the counter/timer: a read of this offset does it.
entries.behaviour: Counter mode stops the count and clears OP3 if OPCR gives it the counter output; timer mode keeps running. Either way ISR bit 3 clears. Returns 0xFF.

entries.name: reset output bits
entries.description: Clears output port bits: each 1 in the byte clears that OPR bit.
entries.behaviour: OPR is ANDed with the inverse of the byte and the output callback receives OPR inverted, so a cleared bit means a high pin. A 0 in the byte changes nothing.
